ruling.recommended_action: Close the fare dispute as no_action: the single off-route segment is exempt as the rider-named stop at Clementi Mall; no mileage refund and no service-fee adjustment is due. No account action on either party.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a metered RydeTAXI Jurong East MRT → NUS, charged $25.33 on the meter with distance $14.65 for 10.39 km and a $1.4100/km rate [F8][F5], so under RD-2 any refund would be the extra_km of an unexcused off-route segment multiplied by that rate [F5][RD-2]. The trace confirms one off-route segment, 14:21–14:31, 3.81 km driven against 2.11 km optimal, +1.70 km [F4][RD-1].

The rider wrote at 14:17, before the segment started at 14:21: "Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes." and the driver answered "Sure" [F9][F10]; the chat record is complete and every message is timestamped [F11]. That is a rider message naming a specific place, sent before the segment, and the car did stop there (stationary 4 min 0 s at 14:23–14:27) [F2]. Under RD-3(a) a rider-named place becomes the destination and the way to reach it is not a detour; the length of the stop or the distance to the place does not reduce the exemption [F9][F2][RD-3]. The rider advocate conceded exactly this in rebuttal and withdrew the mileage claim.

Reading the scope of the agreement under RD-5, "stop at Clementi Mall" names a place, not a road, and nothing in the record names the road the car took or places it on any named road; but the branch that applies is the rider-named stop, whose whole approach is exempt, so the segment is not an "errand of the driver's own" nor an agreed-road segment that needs to be tied to a named road [F4][F9][F2][RD-3][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement is a claim, not consent, and I do not rely on it [F12][RD-5].

RD-4 provides no other excuse and none is needed: no traffic incident was recorded near the route [F15], and the Ayer Rajah Expressway band 4 and Jurong Town Hall Road band 3 records are neither band 1/2 nor tied to the replaced stretch, so they do not exempt anything [F13][F14][RD-4]. On the metered extras, the $1.15 waiting charge for 4.4 min [F6] is meter waiting time on a RydeTAXI stop the rider requested and is chargeable [F6][RD-3]; the $1.47 platform fee is a published add-on [F8][FARE-1]. With no unexcused segment, the RD-2 amount is 0 km × $1.4100/km = $0.00, so the fare stands and the action is no_action [F5][F8][RD-2].

The trace confirms the driver's 90-day profile shows 2 upheld route disputes [F18], but RD-6's flag is an add-on that only operates if the case is established against the driver (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) [F18][RD-6]; here the only segment is exempt, so no flag_account is attached. Profile facts decide nothing on their own [F17][F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement — a stop request, an "Sure", and a description of waiting; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1]. No safety screen renders the ruling unavailable.

segment_findings.reason: Rider message at 14:17, before the segment start (14:21), named a specific place: “Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes.” [F9], driver accepted [F10], chat complete and timestamped [F11], and the car stopped there (stationary 4 min 0 s, 14:23–14:27) [F2]. Under RD-3(a) the rider-named place is the new destination and the whole way there is exempt; neither the stop duration nor the distance of the place reduces the exemption. RD-5 scope: the message names a place, not a road, and no record ties the segment to a named road, so no named-road analysis applies; the rider-named-stop branch governs [RD-3][RD-5][RD-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The geometry of F4 is accepted (one off-route segment, +1.70 km [F4]), but RD-1 treats a segment as a deviation only if no RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 excuse applies; here the rider named Clementi Mall at 14:17 before the segment [F9][F10] and the car stopped there [F2], so RD-3(a) exempts it and no unexcused segment remains [RD-3][RD-1].

The message did name a place, not merely “stop a while”, and a rider-named place is the new destination under RD-3(a); the driving to and from it is performance of the rider's own request, not a driver-chosen route [F9][F10][F2][RD-3]. Nothing in the record places the segment anywhere other than on that errand [F4].

The stationary 4 min 0 s inside a ~10 min segment [F2][F4] does not split the segment: RD-3(a) exempts the named-stop errand as a whole, and no record isolates mileage that reaches nothing; the billed excess of 1.96 km [F5] is absorbed by the exempt segment's 1.70 km [F4][RD-3][RD-2].

The metered structure is as recorded [F5][F8], but RD-2 bites only on an unexcused segment; where the only segment is exempt under RD-3(a) [F4][F9], no unexcused mileage flows into the meter and the $14.65 distance charge stands [RD-2][RD-3].
With the sole segment exempt, the RD-2 amount is 0 km × $1.4100/km = $0.00; the rider advocate also withdrew this $2.40 claim in rebuttal [F4][F5][F8][RD-2][RD-3].

RD-6's flag is an add-on that operates only if the case is established against the driver (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach); no segment survives RD-3(a), so the refund is $0.00 and no flag_account attaches — a profile history cannot decide the case or create the breach [F18][F4][F9][RD-6].

Accepted in part and no longer disputed: the $1.15 waiting charge for 4.4 min [F6] is chargeable meter waiting on a RydeTAXI stop the rider requested [RD-3], and the $1.47 platform fee is a published add-on [F8][FARE-1]; but no refund of the $2.76 excess-distance item arises because the segment was exempt, not because the item was properly justified [F5][F4][RD-2][RD-3].
